newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady on Thursday in lacklustre trade, dealers said.

They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release 1230 GMT release of the U.S. weekly jobless claims and August housing starts and 1400 GMT issue of the September Philadelphia Fed index data.
Weekly jobless claims for the week ended September 14 is forecast to be around 335,000 compared with 338,000 reported in the previous week.
August housing starts is expected to be around 1.445 million annualised units against July's 1.46 million units.
The Philadelphia Fed index for September is expected to ease to 21.0 percent from 21.5 percent in August.
"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning except for some light activity at the short and long ends," a local dealer said.
"Basically, everyone is waiting for the outcome of the (U.S.) Federal Open Market Committee meeting to see whether the Fed will raise it's interest rates or not," he said.
"But some people are waiting for possible direction from tonight's weekly jobless claims, housing starts and Philadelphia Fed index figures," he added.

In day-to-day rates, Thursday/Friday and weekend eased 1/16 percentage point each to a common 5-1/4 5-1/8 percent, respectively. Week-fixed was unchanged from Wednesday's 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent. Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged from Wednesday's 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 and six-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 percent.
But twelve-months rose 1/16 point to 6-1/8 6 percent.
